newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends sharply off on greenback surge.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends sharply off on greenback surge.

text.p: The U.S. dollar's strong showing in Asian markets pulled Taiwan's dollar to a sharply lower close on Monday as last week's sudden Taiwan dollar appreciation failed to take root, dealers said.
The local currency ended at T$27.420 to the U.S. dollar against Saturday's T$27.386 close.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$266 million.
The U.S. dollar rose to a 46-month high against the Japanese yen in Tokyo trade on Monday, exerting strong downward pressure on Taiwan dollar and other Asian currencies.
"The strong U.S. dollar overseas encouraged active selling of the Taiwan dollar, but for the short term the Taiwan dollar still enjoys good support," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
Dealers said demand for the local dollar was expected to rise ahead of the February 7 Chinese lunar new year, limiting its room for further depreciation.
A T$27.38-43 range was seen for Tuesday.
